data.body_html:
Planning a dolphin watching trip in Marbella for 2035? The best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella 2035 is between May and September, when sighting success rates consistently hit 90% or higher. During these months, warm Mediterranean waters (22-26°C) and calm seas bring bottlenose and common dolphins close to the coast, especially around Cabopino and Cala del Faro. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, offering everything from a 2-hour speedboat trip to a full-day luxury charter. Whether you're a family or a group of friends, timing your visit right makes all the difference.

Why May to September Is Prime Dolphin Season

From late spring through early autumn, the Alborán Sea becomes a feeding ground for resident and migratory dolphin pods. Water temperatures rise above 20°C, plankton blooms attract fish, and dolphins follow. In June and July, sightings are almost guaranteed. August can be busier with more boat traffic, but early morning charters still deliver excellent encounters. September sees fewer crowds but equally good conditions, with sea temperatures remaining warm into early October.

Best Time of Day for Dolphin Sightings

Dolphins are most active during the early morning (9:00-11:00) when the sea is flat and they hunt for breakfast. Afternoon sea breezes can create chop that makes spotting harder. We recommend booking a morning slot for the highest chance of success. Our boat rental Marbella options include early departures tailored for wildlife enthusiasts.

Dolphin Species You Can Expect to See

  • Bottlenose dolphins – the most common, often in pods of 10-30, curious and playful near the boat.
  • Common dolphins – smaller and faster, frequently seen in larger groups further offshore.
  • Striped dolphins – less common but occasionally spotted near Estepona.
  • Pilot whales – rare but reported in deeper waters off Marbella.

How Weather and Sea Conditions Affect Sightings

Dolphins prefer calm seas with light winds under 10 knots. Summer months (June-August) offer the most stable weather, with average highs of 28-32°C and minimal swell. Spring and autumn can be good but are more variable. Our skippers monitor real-time conditions and adjust routes to maximise your chances. All charters include safety equipment and insurance, so you're covered whatever the weather.

Recommended Boats for Dolphin Watching

For a quick trip, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are perfect at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. For a longer adventure, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours includes a jet ski. All boats depart from Puerto Banús. See our full fleet for more options.

Tips for a Successful Dolphin Watching Trip

  • Book early morning charters for calmest seas.
  • Bring sunscreen, a hat, and polarised sunglasses to reduce glare.
  • Stay quiet and avoid sudden movements when dolphins are near.
  • Use a camera with a zoom lens – dolphins often surface 10-20 metres away.
  • Contact us via WhatsApp for last-minute availability and weather updates.
